title: DebianSourceReportV1
description:
The §18 comprehensive `DebianSourceReportV1`.

This is the GREEN commit's struct: every §18 top-level group is present, every field the spec names under each group is typed and serialized. The 1C.2 RED commit's struct was the minimal shape; this commit extends it.

binary_packages.description: `binary packages` — every binary package stanza in `debian/control`.

build_metadata.description: `build metadata` — the source paragraph's `Build-Depends`, `Build-Depends-Indep`, `Build-Conflicts`, and the parsed `debhelper-compat` version.

diagnostics.description: Per-check failure / informational lines. Empty when `verdict` is `pass`.

gbp.description: `GBP` — presence of `debian/gbp.conf` and `debian/gbp-dch.conf` and the parsed `[BUILD-DEFAULTS]` branch settings.

identity.description: `identity` — the first-entry changelog block plus the trailer's `Maintainer:` and `Date:` fields.

maintainer_scripts.description: `maintainer scripts` — presence + executable bit for the four canonical scripts, the `triggers` file, and other recognized scripts.

patches.description: `patches` — every patch in `debian/patches/series` with its DEP-3 header.

provenance.description: `provenance` — the candidate's fingerprint, Git commit, Git tree, and the inspector binary's version.

rules.description: `rules` — the `debian/rules` executable bit, the `dh`-style indicator, and the list of `override_*:` targets.

schema_version.description: Always `1` for this revision. Bump on incompatible wire-format changes.

watch.description: `watch` — the parsed `debian/watch` file. `None` when the file is absent.

Autopkgtest.description: One autopkgtest stanza from `debian/tests/control` (§18 tests group).

command.description: Subsequent tokens on the `Tests:` line (the command to run, when it's not the `debian/tests/<name>` default). `None` when the `Tests:` line is just the test name.

depends.description: The `Depends:` field, split into individual entries. Empty when absent.

features.description: The `Features:` field, split into individual tokens. Empty when absent.

name.description: The `Tests:` field, first token (the test name).

restrictions.description: The `Restrictions:` field, split into individual tokens (e.g. `["rw-build-tree"]`). Empty when absent.

BinaryPackage.description: One binary package stanza from `debian/control` (§18 binary packages group).

breaks.description: The `Breaks:` field, split into individual entries. Empty when absent.

conflicts.description: The `Conflicts:` field, split into individual entries. Empty when absent.

depends.description: The `Depends:` field, split into individual entries. Empty when absent.

description.description: The `Description:` field, first paragraph only (the synopsis). Multi-paragraph descriptions are concatenated by dpkg-gencontrol at build time; the report captures the synopsis for observational use.

maintainer.description: The `Maintainer:` field (may differ from the source paragraph's `Maintainer`).

provides.description: The `Provides:` field, split into individual entries. Empty when absent.

replaces.description: The `Replaces:` field, split into individual entries. Empty when absent.

BuildMetadata.description:
The source paragraph's build-related fields (§18 build metadata group).

`Build-Depends` and friends are RFC 822 comma-separated alternation lists; the tool splits them on `,` and trims each entry.

build_conflicts.description: The `Build-Conflicts:` field, split into individual entries. Empty when absent.

build_depends.description: The `Build-Depends:` field, split into individual entries (e.g. `["debhelper-compat (= 13)", "libfoo-dev"]`). Empty when absent.

build_depends_indep.description: The `Build-Depends-Indep:` field, split into individual entries. Empty when absent.

debhelper_compat.description: The `debhelper-compat (= N)` value, parsed out of the `Build-Depends` list. `None` when no `debhelper-compat` entry is present.

ChangelogIdentity.description:
The first-entry identity block from `debian/changelog`.

1C.2 extends this with `maintainer` and `timestamp` (the closing-paren trailer's `Maintainer:` and `Date:` lines). Both new fields are `Option<String>` so a changelog whose trailer is malformed still parses (the report's `diagnostics` carries the `E_CHANGELOG_TRAILER_MALFORMED` line; the verdict aggregates it).

maintainer.description: The trailer's `Maintainer:` line, e.g. `IronMaint Test <test@example.invalid>`. `None` when the trailer has no `Maintainer:` field.

timestamp.description: The trailer's `Date:` line, in the RFC 2822 form `dpkg-parsechangelog` emits (e.g. `Thu, 09 Oct 2026 00:00:00 +0000`). `None` when the trailer has no `Date:` field.

CopyrightInfo.description:
The parsed `debian/copyright` DEP-5 file (§18 copyright group).

The report captures the machine-readable indicator, the `Format:` URL, the count of `Files:` stanzas, and the set of `License:` identifiers across all stanzas (deduplicated, order-preserving).

files_stanza_count.description: The number of `Files:` stanzas in the file. Zero for a header-only copyright file.

format_declaration.description: The `Format:` URL, when present. `None` when the copyright file omits the field.

license_identifiers.description: The set of `License:` values, deduplicated in declaration order. Empty when no `License:` field is present in any stanza.

machine_readable.description: `true` when the `Format:` field's value is a URL (i.e. DEP-5 machine-readable form). `false` for legacy "paragraph prose" form.

Diagnostic.description: A single failure or informational line from the tool.

code.description: A stable, machine-readable error code, e.g. `E_DEBIAN_DIR_MISSING`. Future tools can match on this without parsing the message.

message.description: Human-readable explanation. The tool does not embed the offending value (a) to keep PII out of the report and (b) so the same diagnostic text can serve any fixture.

path.description: The on-disk path that triggered the diagnostic, when applicable (e.g. `debian/`, `debian/changelog`).

GbpBranchSettings.description: The branch / tag settings from `debian/gbp.conf`'s `[BUILD-DEFAULTS]` section.

GbpConfig.description:
The GBP config inventory (§18 GBP group).

The tool reports presence of `debian/gbp.conf` and `debian/gbp-dch.conf` and, when present, the branch / tag settings from the INI-formatted `[BUILD-DEFAULTS]` / `[DCH]` sections. The `branch_settings` block is a structural mirror of the most-commonly-used keys; it is not a full parse of every gbp.conf key.

branch_settings.description: The branch / tag settings parsed from `gbp.conf`. `None` when `gbp.conf` is absent or has no `[BUILD-DEFAULTS]` section.

MaintainerInfo.description:
The source paragraph's `Maintainer:` and `Uploaders:` fields from `debian/control` (§18 maintainers group).

`Maintainer` is the primary contact for the source package; `Uploaders` is a comma-separated list of additional maintainers. The split into a `Vec<String>` makes downstream analysis (e.g. "is this upload co-maintained?") straightforward.

maintainer.description: The `Maintainer:` field, e.g. `IronMaint Test <test@example.invalid>`. Empty when the source paragraph omits it (the `Maintainer` field is mandatory by Policy, but the tool reports what is there).

uploaders.description: The `Uploaders:` field, split on the RFC 822 comma separator. Empty when the source paragraph has no `Uploaders:` field.

MaintainerScripts.description:
The full maintainer-script inventory (§18 maintainer scripts group).

The four canonical scripts are `preinst`/`postinst`/`prerm`/`postrm`. The `triggers` file (a non-executable control file) and "other recognized scripts" (e.g. `postinst-config`, `preinst-base`) are observational — the report captures what is there without claiming anything about what *should* be there.

other_scripts.description: Other recognized scripts in `debian/` (e.g. `preinst-base`, `postinst-config`). Each entry is a `ScriptPresence` keyed by the script's name. Excluded: the four canonical scripts (above), `rules` (covered separately), and the patch series (also covered separately).

triggers.description: `Some` when `debian/triggers` exists. The `triggers` file is a control file (not executable) that declares the package's interest in dpkg triggers.

NamedScript.description: A named maintainer script entry for the `other_scripts` list.

Patch.description: One patch in `debian/patches/series` with its DEP-3 header (§18 patches group).

description.description: The DEP-3 `Description:` header. `None` when the patch file has no DEP-3 header.

last_update.description: The DEP-3 `Last-Update:` header (ISO 8601 date). `None` when absent.

name.description: The patch file name as listed in `series` (e.g. `01-fix-typo.patch`).

Provenance.description:
The provenance block (§18 provenance group).

The candidate fingerprint, Git commit, and Git tree are the candidate's identity (the §18 lines 842-846 requirement). `inspector_version` is the version of the `ironmaint-debian-tool` binary that produced the report, so a downstream consumer can tell which parser version emitted the report.

dh_style.description: `true` when the rules file's first line is `#!/usr/bin/make -f` and the body contains a `dh` invocation. The standard `debhelper` style. The tool's detection is a simple substring check; it does not parse the makefile.

override_targets.description: The names of `override_*:` targets in the rules file. Empty when no override targets are detected.

ScriptPresence.description: One maintainer script's presence + executable bit (§18 maintainer scripts group).

executable.description: `true` when the script file exists and the executable bit is set.

SourceFormat.description:
The canonical string form of `debian/source/format`.

Serialized as the literal file value (`"3.0 (quilt)"`, `"3.0 (native)"`, or the catch-all `"other/legacy"`), not the Rust variant name. A custom `Serialize`/`Deserialize` impl carries the canonical string through; schemars gets the same surface.

oneOf.description: The `3.0 (quilt)` source format. The default for modern Debian source packages.
The `3.0 (native)` source format. Used when the upstream tarball is itself the Debian source.
Any other value in `debian/source/format` (e.g. `1.0`, the native format pre-3.0). The raw string is preserved so an agent can tell what the tool saw.

SourceMetadata.description: The source paragraph's metadata fields from `debian/control` (§18 source metadata group).

standards_version.description: The `Standards-Version:` field (e.g. `4.6.2`). §22's Standards-Version delta evaluator (1D.2) reads this.

oneOf.description: At least one §17 check failed (mismatched name, mismatched version, unparsable `debian/control`, unparsable `debian/changelog`, missing `debian/`, unidentifiable source format, unparsable mandatory metadata). Diagnostics list the specific failure.

The tool could not establish the fact at all: the workspace path is unreadable, an IO error occurred, a parser binary is missing. The §17 rule "parser binary missing → InfrastructureError" lives here.

WatchConfig.description:
The parsed `debian/watch` file (§18 watch group).

The Debian watch file is a small RFC 822-ish grammar: `version=N\n<url-pattern>` with optional `pgpsigurlmangle=` and `opts=...` directives. The tool captures the version, the URL pattern, and any PGP-signature-mangling directive.

pgpsig.description: The `pgpsigurlmangle=...` directive, when present. `None` when absent.

url_pattern.description: The watch file's URL pattern (the first non-comment, non-directive line).
